verdict.rationale: Every deployed LiteLLM proxy serves its own interactive Swagger UI console at its root, generated from the running proxy's OpenAPI spec, so you can explore and call endpoints interactively. The major caveat is that you must deploy a proxy yourself: there is no vendor-hosted public instance, and the docs-site OpenAPI probes all returned 404. missing for 10: a vendor-hosted public interactive reference, documented runnable example requests within the reference, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples

citations.quote: every deployed proxy serves an interactive Swagger UI console at its root
The spec is served at `/openapi.json` and rendered as Swagger UI at `/` by default
There is no vendor-hosted public demo instance today
